newsitem.title: UK: London roads, rail back to normal after alert.
newsitem.headline: London roads, rail back to normal after alert.

text.p: London's road and rail network had returned to normal by Monday afternoon in the wake of a series of security alerts which caused chaos in the morning rush hour, transport sources said.
A spokeswoman for London Transport said all rail and underground stations closed earlier had now re-opened and the network was facing no major delays.
"It's all up and running OK, amazingly," she said.
A spokesman for the Automobile Association said traffic in London was running smoothly.
"There are absolutely no problems -- in fact, it's very quiet," he said. "The normal rush hour is kicking in and there are no major problems."
Heathrow, Gatwick and Luton airports also re-opened after early security alerts, although many flights were still disrupted.
